newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Saab Auto says happy with Q1 Europe sales.
newsitem.headline: Saab Auto says happy with Q1 Europe sales.

text.p: Saab Automobile's managing director Robert Hendry said on Thursday that he was happy with the preliminary sales levels in Europe in the first three months of 1997.
Saab's sales in Britain rose, according to preliminary figures, 24 percent to 4,117 in the first quarter of this year compared to the same period a year ago.
In Germany there was an increase of 15 percent to 1,150 cars and in France a rise of 32 percent to 401 cars in the first quarter.
In March sales in Britain rose by 16 percent to 1,500 cars compared with March last year.
In Germany sales rose by 19 percent to 515 cars and in France sales rose in March by 19 percent 215 cars.
"It is looking very promising in Europe where we have the largest share of our sales," Hendry told a news conference at a car show in Stockholm.
"We have for three years worked with our sales network in Britian which is now giving results."
Up until the year 2000 when Saab Auto has targetted sales of 150,000 cars a year the car maker will continue to work on its sales network in Europe and the U.S..
By then sales in the U.S. will have increased to about 40,000 cars compared with 28,000 in 1996, Hendry said.
Saab Auto is a 50-50 joint venture between Swedish investment company Investor and U.S. automotive group General Motors .
